text: The band gaps (Eg) of NNU-31-M are determined to be 1.85 (Co), 1.82 (Ni), and 1.53 eV (Zn) by their Tauc plots. The visible-light photocatalytic CO2RR was conducted under pure CO2 atmosphere in aqueous solution, without the presence of additional photosensitizer and sacrificial agents. After 24 h of visible-light irradiation, NNU-31-Zn showed an HCOOH yield of 12.51 mmol, while NNU-31-Co and NNU-31-Ni gave 7.17 mmol and 8.22 mmol, respectively. The amount of HCOOH was determined by ion chromatography. The experiments shown in Figure 3a used catalyst weights of 10 or 20 mg. Only HCOOH was detected as the liquid reduction product, and the HCOOH selectivity was approximately 100%. A 13CO2 isotope experiment confirmed that the carbon in HCOOH originated from CO2. O2 was detected as the oxidation product, and H2-18O labeling confirmed that the generated O2 originated from water. The authors report that NNU-31-Zn reaches a CO2-to-HCOOH conversion rate of 26.3 mmol g-1 h-1.

text: Alice-MOF-1 is a Zr-based metal-organic framework containing Zr6-oxo nodes and a perchlorinated L6-Cl12 nanographene ligand. The experimental optical gap is 2.69 eV and the BET surface area is 2397 m2/g. Photocatalytic CO2 reduction experiments using Alice-MOF-1 were performed under white-light irradiation. Figure 3A reports HCOO- and CO yields for Alice-MOF-1 in CO2-sparged 1 M TEOA in 5:1 v/v acetonitrile/water and in CO2-sparged 6:1 v/v acetonitrile/water without TEOA. When TEOA was used as the sacrificial electron donor, formate was the main product. A small amount of CO (0.36 micromol) was also formed over the course of the reaction. C1 products were also observed in the absence of TEOA, showing that water can serve as the terminal electron source. GC-MS analysis after irradiation with H2-18O showed 18O2 formation, and 13CO2 labeling confirmed that the carbon source for formate and CO was CO2.

text: AUBM-4 is a zirconium-based metal-organic framework incorporating the photoactive bis(4'-(4-carboxyphenyl)-terpyridine)ruthenium(II) linker, Ru(cptpy)2. The crystal structure contains ZrO8 secondary building units linked by Ru(cptpy)2 struts, and the optical band gap of AUBM-4 is 1.88 eV. For photocatalytic CO2 reduction, 40 mL of acetonitrile and 10 mL of triethanolamine (TEOA) were added to a 100 mL enclosed two-necked pear-shaped flask containing 20 mg of AUBM-4. The mixture was purged with argon to remove dissolved oxygen and was irradiated at room temperature from a distance of 20 cm using a 150 W xenon lamp through an AM 1.5 filter with continuous stirring. The reaction medium was saturated with CO2. Formate was quantified by ion chromatography. Formate production reached 44 micromol after 6 h, corresponding to an average formation rate of 7.3 micromol/h and a mass-normalized conversion rate of 366 micromol g-1 h-1. No significant methane or other hydrocarbon gas products were detected after 6 h. A 13CO2 experiment confirmed that the carbon in the produced formate originated from CO2.
